standard_prerequisites.name: Property (P) resolutions compute derived tensor
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same unit, the construction behind equation equation-plain-versus-derived-algebras and Lemma lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general-algebra
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof chooses a property (P) resolution P -> (A tensor_R B)_B and works with the plain tensor representatives of the derived functors as in that construction.

standard_prerequisites.name: K-flat base change
standard_prerequisites.use: Final step (source line 6090): tensoring a quasi-isomorphism with a K-flat complex of R-modules preserves quasi-isomorphism, so P tensor_R C -> A tensor_R B tensor_R C is a quasi-isomorphism when C is K-flat.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 6066-6074): if C is K-flat as a complex of R-modules, then the map of equation equation-plain-versus-derived-algebras is an isomorphism and the conclusion of Lemma lemma-compose-tensor-functors-general-algebra is valid.

Resolution reduction (proof lines 6076-6084): choose a quasi-isomorphism P -> (A tensor_R B)_B of differential graded B-modules with P of property (P); by the construction it suffices to show P tensor_B (B tensor_R C) -> (A tensor_R B) tensor_B (B tensor_R C) is a quasi-isomorphism.
Reassociation (lines 6084-6088): by associativity of the tensor product this is equivalent to P tensor_R C -> A tensor_R B tensor_R C being a quasi-isomorphism.
K-flat conclusion (lines 6088-6091): since P -> A tensor_R B is a quasi-isomorphism and C is K-flat as a complex of R-modules, the More on Algebra K-flat lemma gives the required quasi-isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Replace (A tensor_R B)_B by its property (P) resolution.
Reassociate the plain tensor products to a single tensor over R.
Apply the K-flat criterion for tensoring quasi-isomorphisms.
difficulty_reason: K-flatness lemma (statement 6066-6074, proof 6076-6091): K-flatness of C makes the plain composition of tensor functors compute the derived one - the proof is a resolution reduction followed by an explicit reassociation and the standard K-flat criterion; each step is stated with its justification; no step is omitted. H2: short reduction with standard K-flat input.
